name: Psi, Declassified
claim: Declassified government programs (CIA/DIA 'Stargate') supposedly proved remote viewing and psychic perception are real, trainable skills that mainstream science suppresses or ignores.
born_note: Estimate based on the 1995 CIA declassification of the Stargate program and the ensuing media wave; revived by podcasts since ~2020. (model estimate, pending audit)

explanations.layman: Some shows say the US government secretly proved people can 'see' faraway places with their minds, and that you can learn it too. The proof usually points to old declassified files. Skeptics say those files show weak, unrepeatable results that the government shut down for good reason. It matters because the same 'hidden truth' framing sells courses, books and belief.
explanations.intermediate: Mechanism: declassified Stargate documents plus insider testimony are treated as institutional validation, then paired with trainable 'protocols.' Camp one (proponents, ex-program participants, consciousness researchers) argues effect sizes are small but real and suppressed. Camp two (skeptics, statisticians) points to the 1995 AIR review, loose blinding, and judging bias. Podcasts amplify by hosting proponents without adversarial review.
explanations.expert: Audit framing: clock is 'science will confirm within years' — perpetually unmet since 1995. Falsifiers: pre-registered, blinded replication with independent judging; the AIR/Hyman-Utts split is the canonical fork. Incentives: course sales, book deals, podcast attention economics, legacy-defense by former program staff. Lifecycle: mature legacy narrative in periodic revival, currently boosted by consciousness-and-UAP adjacency.
